options: Counter-clockwise and inward
Counter-clockwise and outward
Clockwise and outward
Directly from the center to the edges

bank.question: International Code Flag 'A' (Alpha), which is a swallow-tailed flag divided vertically into white (hoist) and blue (fly). What is the meaning of this International Code Flag?
bank.explanation: Flag 'A' (Alpha) is blue and white and indicates 'I have a diver down; keep well clear at slow speed.'
options: I am dragging my anchor
I require a pilot
I am carrying dangerous cargo
I have a diver down; keep well clear

bank.question: According to the crossing rule for two power-driven vessels on a collision course, which vessel is the 'Give-way' vessel?
bank.explanation: Under ColRegs Rule 15, when two power-driven vessels are crossing, the vessel which has the other on her starboard side must keep out of the way.
options: The vessel which has the other on her starboard side
The vessel which has the other on her port side
The larger vessel
The vessel travelling at a slower speed

bank.question: A pillar buoy with alternating red and white vertical stripes. It is topped with a single red spherical topmark. What type of mark is represented by these colours and topmark?
bank.explanation: A Safe Water Mark has vertical red and white stripes and a single red sphere topmark. It has clean water all around it
options: Safe Water Mark
Isolated Danger Mark
South Cardinal Mark
Port Hand Mark

bank.question: Where is a North Cardinal mark placed in relation to the danger it identifies?
bank.explanation: Cardinal marks are named after the quadrant in which they are placed; a North mark is placed to the North of the danger
options: To the North of the danger
To the South of the danger
Exactly on top of the danger
To the West of the danger

bank.question: A night view of a vessel showing a red sidelight (port), a green sidelight (starboard), and two white masthead lights, with the aft white light higher than the forward one. What is the size and type of the vessel showing these lights at night?
bank.explanation: At night, a power-driven vessel over 50m shows two masthead lights, sidelights, and a sternlight. The higher second masthead light is aft
options: Sailing vessel under 20m
Power-driven vessel less than 50m in length
Power-driven vessel over 50m in length
Vessel engaged in trawling

bank.question: When entering a UK harbour from the sea, which shape represents the Starboard Hand Lateral Mark?
bank.explanation: When entering a harbour in IALA Region A (UK), the starboard side of the channel is marked by green conical buoys.
options: A green conical buoy
A red can buoy
A yellow spherical buoy
A white pillar buoy

bank.question: A power-driven vessel seen from the side towing another vessel. A black diamond day shape is displayed on the towing vessel where it can best be seen. What does this black diamond day shape indicate on a towing vessel?
bank.explanation: The diamond shape indicates a vessel engaged in towing where the length of the tow exceeds 200 metres
options: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A vessel engaged in a tow exceeding 200m
A vessel engaged in fishing with gear extending 150m
A vessel at anchor

bank.question: What is the definition of 'Magnetic Variation'?
bank.explanation: Variation is the angle between True North and Magnetic North, caused by the Earth's magnetic field
options: The difference between Course Over Ground and Heading
The angular difference between True North and Magnetic North
The error caused by local magnetic fields on the boat
The distance between two lines of longitude

bank.question: A rectangular white flag with a red saltire (diagonal cross) from corner to corner, flying from a mast. What is the meaning of this International Code Flag?
bank.explanation: The 'V' flag indicates 'I require assistance' and is a standard International Code of Signals flag
options: I have a diver down; keep well clear
I am moving to port
I require assistance
Man overboard

bank.question: Under ColRegs Rule 12, when two sailing vessels are on the same tack, which vessel is required to 'Give-way'?
bank.explanation: Under ColRegs Rule 12, when two sailing vessels have the wind on the same side, the vessel to windward shall keep out of the way of the vessel to leeward.
options: The vessel to windward
The vessel to leeward
The vessel with the main engine running
The larger vessel

bank.question: A pillar-shaped buoy, coloured black with one horizontal red band. The topmark consists of two black spheres one above the other. Identify this buoy and the correct action to take?
bank.explanation: Isolated danger marks are positioned over hazards with navigable water all around them. Pass on either side but give a wide berth
options: Isolated danger mark; pass on either side but with caution
Emergency wreck buoy; pass to the North
Special mark; marks a recreation zone
Safe water mark; keep to the starboard side

bank.question: What day-shape must a vessel 'Restricted in her Ability to Manoeuvre' (RAM) exhibit?
bank.explanation: Restricted in Ability to Manoeuvre (RAM) vessels display a ball-diamond-ball shape. Examples include cable layers or buoy tenders
options: Two black balls
A black cylinder
A single black cone pointing down
A ball, a diamond, and a ball in a vertical line

bank.question: The night-time profile of a vessel showing three green lights in a vertical triangular formation (one at the masthead and one on each end of the foreyard). What type of vessel is indicated by these three green lights?
bank.explanation: Three green lights in a vertical line indicate a vessel engaged in mine clearance operations. Keep well clear
options: A pilot vessel on duty
A vessel engaged in mine clearance
A vessel constrained by her draught
A trawler hauling nets

bank.question: Which line prevents a boat from moving forward along the pontoon when strongly hit by wind from astern?
bank.explanation: The stern spring runs from the stern of the boat forward to the pontoon to prevent the vessel from moving or surging forward.
options: The stern spring, running from the stern of the boat forward to the pontoon
The bow spring, running from the bow of the boat aft to the pontoon
A bow line, running from the bow forward to the pontoon
A stern line, running from the stern aft to the pontoon

bank.question: An extract from a nautical chart showing a magenta circular dashed line with a large magenta exclamation mark in the centre. What does this chart symbol signify?
bank.explanation: The Magenta '!' inside a circle indicates a 'Precautionary Area' where ships must navigate with particular caution, often near Traffic Separation Schemes
options: Entry prohibited area
Firing practice area
Recommended anchorage
Precautionary area; navigate with caution

bank.question: When do the largest tidal ranges (Spring Tides) typically occur?
bank.explanation: Spring tides occur when the Sun and Moon are aligned, resulting in the greatest tidal range
options: Just after a New Moon or Full Moon
During the first and third quarters of the lunar cycle
Only during the summer months in the UK
When the Moon is at its furthest point from Earth

bank.question: A pillar buoy with a black top band, a central yellow band, and a black bottom band. The topmark is two black cones with points together (wasp-waisted). Identify this cardinal mark and the safe side on which to pass it?
bank.explanation: A West Cardinal mark has a yellow band in the middle of two black bands and 'point-to-point' cones. Pass to the West
options: West Cardinal; pass to the West
East Cardinal; pass to the East
South Cardinal; pass to the South
Preferred channel to port

bank.question: Which buoy marks a landfall at the start of a channel where there is deep water in all directions?
bank.explanation: The Safe Water Mark (identified by vertical red/white stripes and a red sphere topmark) indicates that there is navigable water all around the mark, making it suitable as a landfall buoy.
options: A Safe Water Mark
A Port Hand Mark
A Starboard Hand Mark
A Cardinal Mark

bank.question: At night, a vessel showing two all-round red lights in a vertical line and, in addition, the white all-round anchor lights. What does this light configuration signify?
bank.explanation: A vessel aground shows two red lights in a vertical line plus her usual anchor lights (white)
options: A vessel hampered by her draught
An NUC vessel making way through the water
A vessel aground
A vessel engaged in underwater operations

bank.question: What is the purpose of a 'Sector Light' on a chart?
bank.explanation: A sector light uses different colours (usually Red, White, and Green) to indicate safe or dangerous areas for navigation
options: A light that flashes only once per minute
A light that is only visible during the day
A light that shows different colours over specific arcs of the horizon
A light used only to mark the entrance to a marina

bank.question: A close-up of a depth soundings area on a nautical chart with the abbreviation 'Co' printed near a depth number. On a British Admiralty chart, what does the abbreviation 'Co' mean?
bank.explanation: The 'Co' indicates Cobbles on the seabed, which can provide moderate holding but may be uneven
options: Coral
Cobbles
Coarse sand
Copper deposit

bank.question: Which type of buoy indicates a small hazard that has navigable water all around it?
bank.explanation: An Isolated Danger Mark is placed over a hazard surrounded by navigable water and is identified by two black spheres as a topmark.
options: Isolated Danger Mark
Lateral Mark
Safe Water Mark
Special Mark

bank.question: A nautical chart extract showing a depth of 12 metres with a small lowercase 'm' underneath the digits. What does the abbreviation 'm' indicate about the nature of the seabed?
bank.explanation: The 'm' signifies the seabed is made of Mud, which generally offers good holding ground for anchors
options: Metres (unit of height)
Middle of channel
Mixed ground
Mud

bank.question: In a crossing situation between two power-driven vessels, which one is generally the 'give-way' vessel?
bank.explanation: Under COLREGs Rule 15, in a crossing situation between two power-driven vessels, the vessel which has the other on her own starboard side shall keep out of the way
options: The vessel on the starboard side must give way
The vessel which has the other on her own starboard side must give way
Both vessels must turn to port immediately
The smaller vessel must always give way to the larger vessel

bank.question: A silhouette of a ship at night showing two white masthead lights (steaming lights) at different heights, and red/green sidelights. The presence of two masthead lights at different heights indicates what?
bank.explanation: A vessel of 50m or more must show two masthead lights; the aft one is higher than the forward one. 225-degree arc of visibility
options: A power-driven vessel less than 7m in length
A sailing vessel using an engine
A power-driven vessel 50m or more in length
A pilot vessel at anchor

bank.question: According to ColRegs Rule 30, what light configuration indicates a vessel under 50m that is currently at anchor at night?
bank.explanation: Under ColRegs Rule 30, a vessel at anchor must show one all-round white light where it can best be seen (for vessels under 50m).
options: One all-round white light
Two all-round white lights vertically
One all-round red light
One masthead light and sidelights

bank.question: A spar buoy, yellow on top and black on bottom. The topmark features two black cones both pointing downwards. Identify this mark and the safe side on which to pass it?
bank.explanation: This is a South Cardinal buoy (two cones pointing down). In a buoyage direction, pass to the South of this mark
options: South Cardinal; pass to the South
North Cardinal; pass to the North
East Cardinal; pass to the East
Special mark; avoid the area

bank.question: What is the primary purpose of 'Springs' when mooring a vessel alongside?
bank.explanation: Springs are used to prevent a vessel from moving fore and aft (backwards or forwards) along the quay
options: To stop the boat moving away from the quay sideways
To hold the bow onto the wind only
To provide extra weight to the anchor chain
To prevent the boat from moving fore and aft along the pontoon

bank.question: Night view of a vessel showing a red light directly above a green light, both all-round, at or near the masthead. No other lights are visible. What type of vessel is displaying these lights?
bank.explanation: A vessel seen from ahead showing a red over green light is a sailing vessel under way. No white masthead light is visible
options: A pilot vessel under way
A sailing vessel under way
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A trawler fishing

bank.question: Which knot is most secure and least likely to jam under heavy load when mooring a boat to a harbour ring for several days?
bank.explanation: The Round Turn and Two Half Hitches is the preferred knot for securing a boat to a ring or post because it is easy to undo even after being under heavy load.
options: Round Turn and Two Half Hitches
Bowline
Cleat Hitch
Clove Hitch

bank.question: A day-time scene of a motor vessel at sea. From its mast, it is flying two solid black circular shapes (balls) arranged one above the other in a vertical line. What does this day shape configuration indicate?
bank.explanation: Two black spheres (balls) in a vertical line indicate a vessel 'not under command' (NUC), meaning it cannot maneuver as required
options: A vessel aground
A vessel not under command
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A vessel engaged in fishing

bank.question: In an Admiralty Almanac, what is defined as a 'Standard Port'?
bank.explanation: Standard Port tide tables provide the core data, while Secondary Port data is derived by applying time and height differences
options: A port for which daily tide predictions are provided in the almanac
A port that can only be accessed at High Water
A small harbour that does not require a pilot
A port used only for emergency stops and refuelling

bank.question: A buoy painted yellow with a single broad black horizontal band around the middle. The topmark consists of two black cones, one pointing up and one pointing down, with their apexes touching (hourglass shape). Identify this buoy and the safe side on which to pass it?
bank.explanation: A yellow buoy with a black horizontal band and two cones pointing towards each other is an East Cardinal mark. Pass to the East
options: West Cardinal mark - pass to the West
North Cardinal mark - pass to the North
East Cardinal mark - pass to the East
South Cardinal mark - pass to the South

bank.question: What symbol is used on a chart to plot an 'Estimated Position' (EP) after applying the effects of tide and leeway to a Dead Reckoning (DR) track?
bank.explanation: An Estimated Position (EP) is marked on a chart using a triangle with a dot in the centre, often with a line showing the direction of the water track.
options: A triangle with a dot in the centre
A cross
A circle with a dot in the centre
A square

bank.question: A night scene showing the silhouette of a large ship. On its mast, it displays three red all-round lights in a vertical line. Port and starboard sidelights are also visible. What does this light configuration indicate at night?
bank.explanation: A vessel displaying three red lights in a vertical line is 'constrained by her draught' and cannot deviate from her course
options: A vessel constrained by her draught
A vessel engaged in pilotage duty
A vessel aground
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre

bank.question: What is the most reliable method to check your steering compass for 'Deviation' while underway?
bank.explanation: The 'Transit' is the most accurate way to check compass error while at sea using two fixed, charted objects
options: Using a GPS handheld unit
Lining up two charted fixed objects in a 'Transit'
Comparing the reading to another boat's compass
Checking the depth of water against the chart

bank.question: A snippet of a nautical chart showing a small circle of dots. Inside the circle is the abbreviation 'Wk' and a depth sounding of '4.5'. What does this chart symbol and depth indicate?
bank.explanation: The symbol 'Wk' with a circle of dots and a depth number indicates a wreck that is fully submerged but has been surveyed
options: A wreck showing above the water level
A dangerous rock at chart datum
A wreck over which the depth is unknown
A submerged wreck with a known depth of 4.5m

bank.question: Which description accurately depicts a rope correctly secured with a Cleat Hitch?
bank.explanation: The Cleat Hitch is the correct way to secure a line to a cleat, involving a full turn around the base followed by a figure-eight pattern.
options: A full turn around the base followed by a figure-eight pattern
Multiple figure-eight turns only
A series of half hitches
A single round turn

bank.question: A yacht at anchor in a bay during the day. Hanging from the forestay at the front of the boat is a single solid black sphere. What is indicated by the day shape shown on this yacht?
bank.explanation: A single black ball is the day shape for a vessel at anchor
options: The vessel is fishing
The vessel is under sail and motor
The vessel is at anchor motor-sailing
The vessel is aground

bank.question: From which datum are the heights of lighthouses and mountains usually measured on an Admiralty Chart?
bank.explanation: Charted heights for lights and mountains are measured from Mean High Water Springs (MHWS) to ensure minimum clearance is known
options: Chart Datum (CD)
Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT)
Mean High Water Springs (MHWS)
Mean Sea Level (MSL)

bank.question: A large container ship at sea. On its main mast, it is displaying a large, solid black cylinder day shape. Identify the meaning of this day shape?
bank.explanation: A cylinder day shape is specifically used by vessels constrained by their draught to indicate their status during the day
options: Vessel constrained by her draught
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Vessel at anchor
Vessel engaged in underwater operations

bank.question: Which mooring line prevents the boat from moving backward when moored in a strong current pushing from ahead?
bank.explanation: The Stern Spring runs from the stern of the boat forward to the pontoon, preventing the vessel from moving aft while moored.
options: Stern Spring
Bow Spring
Head line
Stern line

bank.question: A green buoy, conical in shape, floating in a channel. It has no topmark and is plain green. Identify this buoy and how you should pass it when entering a harbour?
bank.explanation: A green conical buoy is a starboard hand lateral mark; when entering a harbour (direction of buoyage), it should be kept to the starboard side
options: Port hand mark - leave to port when entering harbour
Starboard hand mark - leave to starboard when entering harbour
Preferred channel mark to port
Special mark - caution required

bank.question: What day-shape must a sailing vessel display when proceeding under power with sails hoisted?
bank.explanation: A sailing vessel using its engine is legally a power-driven vessel and must show a cone (point down) to indicate this to others
options: A black cone, point downwards
A black ball
A black cylinder
A black diamond

bank.question: A night view of a vessel. In addition to normal steaming lights, it displays three all-round lights in a vertical line: Red on top, White in the middle, and Red on the bottom. What is the status of a vessel displaying these lights?
bank.explanation: A red-white-red vertical light sequence indicates a vessel Restricted in Her Ability to Manoeuvre (RAM), such as a dredger or cable layer
options: A vessel at anchor
A vessel engaged in pilotage duty
A vessel constrained by her draught
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre

bank.question: Which description indicates the correct 'Topmark' for a West Cardinal Mark?
bank.explanation: A West Cardinal mark has two black cones pointing towards each other (point-to-point) and indicates the safest water is to the West of the mark.
options: Two black cones pointing towards each other (point-to-point)
Two black cones pointing upwards
Two black cones pointing downwards
A single red sphere

bank.question: A section of a nautical chart. Near a depth sounding of 12 metres, the letters 'Sh' are printed in lower case/italics. What does the abbreviation 'Sh' indicate on a nautical chart?
bank.explanation: The abbreviation 'Sh' on a chart stands for 'Shells', indicating the composition of the seabed in that area
options: Shallow water entry
Shingle seabed
Shells on the seabed
Sharp rocks below

bank.question: What is 'Chart Datum' (CD) used to define on a nautical chart?
bank.explanation: CH is Chart Datum, while MHWS is Mean High Water Springs. Heights of lights and landmarks are measured from HAT/MHWS, but depths and drying heights are related to Chart Datum
options: The height of the highest astronomical tide
The lowest astronomical tide likely to occur
The average depth of the sea over 18 years
The maximum depth at Mean High Water Springs

bank.question: A night-time view showing a vessel (the tow) behind another. This vessel displays only its red and green sidelights. No white masthead lights are visible on this specific vessel. What is the status of the second vessel being moved in this night scene?
bank.explanation: A vessel being towed is indicated by its sidelights and a sternlight, but no masthead (steaming) lights
options: A sailing vessel under motor
A vessel being towed
A pilot vessel on duty
A vessel less than 7 metres in length

bank.question: What is the correct light configuration at night for a vessel 'Not Under Command' (NUC)?
bank.explanation: A vessel Not Under Command (NUC) is identified at night by two all-round red lights in a vertical line.
options: Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
One all-round white light
One masthead light and sidelights
Two all-round white lights in a vertical line

bank.question: A buoy painted black on the top half and yellow on the bottom half. It has a topmark of two black cones, both pointing upwards. Identify this mark and the safe side on which to pass it?
bank.explanation: Two black cones with apexes pointing up indicate a North Cardinal mark. It should be passed to the North to stay in safe water
options: North Cardinal mark - pass to the North
South Cardinal mark - pass to the South
West Cardinal mark - pass to the West
Isolated danger mark - pass well clear

bank.question: What weather pattern is typically associated with the approach of a Warm Front?
bank.explanation: Warm air is forced up over cold air at a warm front, causing widespread cloud and prolonged, steady rain before the front passes
options: Rapidly falling temperature and heavy thunderstorms
Clear blue skies and light winds from the north
Layered cloud and steady, persistent rainfall
Rising barometer and visibility decreasing to fog

bank.question: A night scene of a small boat. On its mast, it has two all-round lights in a vertical line: a white light on top and a red light directly below it. Sidelights are also visible. What type of vessel is indicated by these lights?
bank.explanation: A white light over a red light in a vertical line indicates a vessel on pilotage duty. 'White over red, pilot ahead'
options: Vessel engaged in fishing
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Vessel on pilotage duty
Vessel at anchor

bank.question: Which mooring line primarily prevents the boat from moving astern when the wind is blowing strongly from the bow?
bank.explanation: The aft spring runs from the stern of the boat forward to the pontoon, preventing the vessel from moving backwards along the berth.
options: Aft spring
Forward spring
Head line
Stern line

bank.question: A yellow pillar-shaped buoy with a yellow 'X' shaped topmark. No lights are shown in this daytime view. Identify this buoy type based on its shape and topmark?
bank.explanation: A yellow cross topmark on a buoy indicates a Special Mark, used to mark specific features like outfalls or racing marks
options: Lateral Mark
Special Mark
Emergency Wreck Buoy Racing Mark
Isolated Danger Mark

bank.question: Moving 'with the flood' into a UK harbour, what is the shape and colour of a Port Hand Mark?
bank.explanation: Lateral marks indicate the edges of a channel. In IALA Region A (UK), red port marks are on the left when entering from sea
options: A red can shape
A green cone shape
A red cone shape
A green can shape

bank.question: A snippet of a nautical chart showing a small drying height area with the abbreviation 'Wk' (wreck) and the symbol for a rock or small island. What does this specific nautical chart symbol represent?
bank.explanation: The white 'I' symbol indicates an island, and 'Wk' stands for a wreck; the surrounding dots indicate it is always covers/uncovers
options: A wreck that is always covered by water
A wreck that dries at low water
A safe water mark near a wreck
A dangerous rock in the vicinity of a harbour

bank.question: Which description correctly identifies a South Cardinal Mark?
bank.explanation: A South Cardinal mark has two cones pointing downwards and a yellow band above a black band on the hull.
options: Two cones pointing downwards and a yellow band above a black band on the hull
Two cones pointing upwards and a black band above a yellow band on the hull
Two cones pointing towards each other and an all-black hull
Two cones pointing away from each other and an all-yellow hull

bank.question: The night-time profile of a vessel showing two vertical all-round red lights. No other lights are visible. According to ColRegs, what is the status of a vessel displaying these lights?
bank.explanation: A vessel 'Not Under Command' (NUC) is required to show two all-round red lights in a vertical line when making way
options: Vessel aground
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Vessel not under command
Vessel engaged in pilotage duty

bank.question: In a tidal almanac, what is a 'Secondary Port'?
bank.explanation: A secondary port uses time and height differences applied to a designated Standard Port to calculate its specific tide times
options: Port with its own full tidal curve and table in the Almanac
A port that follows a different time zone from the rest of the UK
A port where tidal calculations are derived from a nearby Standard Port
A port that only allows entry during Spring Tides

bank.question: A large commercial vessel seen from the side displaying a single black cylinder day shape in the rigging. What does this day shape indicate about the vessel's movement?
bank.explanation: A cylinder day shape signifies a vessel constrained by her draught, unable to deviate from her course
options: Vessel constrained by her draught
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Vessel at anchor
Vessel engaged in underwater operations

bank.question: Two sailing vessels are on a collision course with the wind coming from different sides. Which vessel must give way?
bank.explanation: Under ColRegs Rule 12, when two sailing vessels have the wind on different sides, the vessel with the wind on the port side must give way.
options: The vessel with the wind on its port side.
The vessel with the wind on its starboard side.
The vessel sailing closer to the wind.
The vessel that is larger.

bank.question: A green buoy with a conical (pointed) top, floating in a channel. You are entering a harbour (with the flood tide). On which side should you leave this mark?
bank.explanation: In IALA Region A, a green conical buoy marks the starboard side of the channel when entering with the flood tide
options: Port hand mark, leave to port when entering
Starboard hand mark, leave to port when entering
Port hand mark, leave to starboard when entering
Starboard hand mark, leave to starboard when entering

bank.question: A power-driven vessel is overtaking a sailing vessel from directly astern. Which vessel is the 'give-way' vessel?
bank.explanation: Under Rule 13, any vessel overtaking another must keep out of the way of the vessel being overtaken, regardless of sail or power
options: The sailing vessel because it is under sail
The overtaking vessel (power-driven)
Neither; both must turn at least 45 degrees to starboard
The sailing vessel because it is slower

bank.question: A symbol of a tall tower with radiating lines and the abbreviation 'R' next to it on a coastal chart. What is the meaning of this landmark symbol on a British Admiralty chart?
bank.explanation: The symbol 'R' or 'Ro' on a chart indicates a Radio or TV mast, often used as a conspicuous landmark for bearings
options: Rescue Station
Radio or TV Mast
Radar Station
Refuge for small craft

bank.question: You need to quickly tie a temporary line to a vertical timber post on a pier. Which knot is most suitable?
bank.explanation: A clove hitch is a quick and effective way to temporarily secure a line to a vertical post or rail.
options: Clove Hitch
Bowline
Figure-of-eight knot
Reef Knot

bank.question: Lights at night showing a green all-round light directly above a white all-round light. Red and green sidelights are also visible below. What activity is this vessel engaged in based on these lights?
bank.explanation: A green light over a white light in a vertical line signifies a vessel engaged in trawling
options: Vessel engaged in pilotage duty
Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling
Vessel engaged in trawling
Sailing vessel underway

bank.question: What does the term 'Veering' mean in a UK Shipping Forecast?
bank.explanation: In the Northern Hemisphere, a 'Veering' wind shifts clockwise (e.g., SW to W), while 'Backing' describes an anti-clockwise shift
options: The wind direction is shifting clockwise
The wind speed is increasing rapidly
The wind direction is shifting anti-clockwise
The wind is moving from sea to land (sea breeze)

bank.question: A yacht at anchor in a bay, displaying one black ball in the forward part of the vessel. What does the day shape shown on this vessel signify?
bank.explanation: A black ball is the standard day shape to indicate a vessel is at anchor
options: Vessel under power and sail
Vessel at anchor
Vessel aground
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre

bank.question: You are navigating a power-driven vessel and see another power-driven vessel approaching head-on. According to ColRegs, which vessel(s) must alter course to starboard?
bank.explanation: Under ColRegs Rule 14, when two power-driven vessels meet on head-on courses, both must alter course to starboard, meaning each passes on the port side of the other.
options: Both vessels must alter course to starboard.
Only your vessel must alter course to starboard.
Only the other vessel must alter course to starboard.
Neither vessel needs to alter course if they maintain speed.

bank.question: A ship displaying three shapes in a vertical line (ball-diamond-ball) on its mast, and an additional two diamonds in a vertical line on its starboard side. What is indicated by the two diamonds shown on the side of this vessel?
bank.explanation: Two black diamonds in a vertical line indicate the safe side to pass a vessel restricted in its ability to manoeuvre
options: The vessel is at anchor
There is an obstruction on this side; do not pass
The vessel is constrained by its draught
This is the safe side to pass the vessel

bank.question: What is the topmark of a West Cardinal mark?
bank.explanation: A West Cardinal mark has two black cones pointing towards each other (point-to-point) and a yellow/black/yellow horizontal band pattern
options: Cones pointing upwards
Cones pointing downwards
Cones pointing towards each other (points together)
Cones pointing away from each other (bases together)

bank.question: A spherical buoy with red and white vertical stripes and a single red ball topmark. Identify this buoy and its purpose?
bank.explanation: A Safe Water Mark (red/white stripes) indicates that there is navigable water all around the mark
options: Safe Water Mark
Isolated Danger Mark
Mid-channel Port Hand Mark
South Cardinal Mark

bank.question: You need to join two ropes of different diameters securely together. Which knot is most suitable for this purpose?
bank.explanation: The Sheet Bend is the standard knot used for joining two ropes together, especially if they are of unequal thickness.
options: Sheet Bend
Reef Knot
Fisherman's Bend
Granny Knot

bank.question: A section of a chart with the letters 'f S' printed near a depth sounder. What does the abbreviation 'f' indicate regarding the nature of the seabed?
bank.explanation: The 'f' abbreviation indicates a seabed composed of fine-grained material (Fine Sand)
options: Foul Ground, Sand
Firm Sand
Fine Sand
Flat Seabed, Sand

bank.question: In navigation, what does the 'Set' of a tidal stream refer to?
bank.explanation: Set is the compass direction towards which the tide is flowing, whereas Drift is the speed/rate of that flow
options: The speed of the tidal stream in knots
The direction towards which the tidal stream is flowing
The distance the tide has moved the vessel over ground
The direction from which the wind is blowing

bank.question: A nautical chart excerpt showing a sheltered area of water with a small pictorial symbol of a sailing yacht inside it. What does this chart symbol signify for a coastal navigator?
bank.explanation: The symbol of a yacht inside a box usually indicates a marina or a dedicated yacht basin
options: Anchorage for small craft
Marina or Yacht Basin
Sailing club with no mooring
Restricted area for yachts

bank.question: You are navigating near a hazard and need to pass to the East of it. Which cardinal mark indicates the East?
bank.explanation: An East Cardinal mark has two cones pointing away from each other (base to base) and a black-yellow-black colour sequence.
options: An East Cardinal mark with two cones pointing away from each other (base to base) and a black-yellow-black colour sequence.
A North Cardinal mark with two cones pointing upwards.
A South Cardinal mark with two cones pointing downwards.
A West Cardinal mark with two cones pointing towards each other (point to point).

bank.question: A North Cardinal buoy with a black band above a yellow band and two triangles (cones) both pointing upwards as the topmark. Identify this buoy and the safe side on which to pass it?
bank.explanation: A North Cardinal mark has two cones pointing up. You should pass to the North of this mark to remain in safe water
options: East Cardinal - Pass to the East
North Cardinal - Pass to the North
West Cardinal - Pass to the West
South Cardinal - Pass to the South

bank.question: Which lights must a 12-metre power-driven vessel exhibit at night when underway?
bank.explanation: Under Rule 23, power-driven vessels under 50m must show a masthead light (white), sidelights (red/green), and a sternlight (white)
options: Red and green sidelights only
All-round white light and red/green sidelights
A single all-round yellow light
Masthead light, sidelights, and a sternlight

bank.question: A profile view of a large commercial container ship displaying a black cylinder day shape in its rigging. What is the status of a vessel displaying this day shape?
bank.explanation: A cylinder day shape indicates a vessel constrained by her draught, meaning she is severely restricted in her ability to deviate from the course she is following
options: Constrained by her draught
Restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Aground
Trawling

bank.question: In a distress situation where you must abandon ship, which satellite-based emergency beacon should you activate to alert search and rescue services?
bank.explanation: An EPIRB (Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon) is used to alert search and rescue services via satellite in the event of an emergency.
options: EPIRB (Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon)
SART (Search and Rescue Transponder)
PLB (Personal Locator Beacon)
VHF radio

bank.question: A white hull sailing yacht in a bay, with a single black sphere (ball) suspended from the forestay near the bow. What does the black ball shape on this vessel indicate?
bank.explanation: A single ball day shape indicates a vessel at anchor. This signifies the vessel is not under way
options: Vessel under sail and power
Vessel aground outdoor
Vessel at anchor
Vessel engaged in diving operations

bank.question: In pilotage, what is a 'Transit' (also known as a Range)?
bank.explanation: A 'Transit' is a highly accurate position line formed when two charted objects are observed to be perfectly in line
options: When two charted objects are observed to be in one line
The point where the vessel crosses a major shipping lane
A bearing taken from a single fixed object on the shore
The path of a vessel over the seabed including leeway

bank.question: A dark night scene with two vertical lights on a mast: the top one is green and the bottom one is white. Red/green sidelights are not visible. What type of vessel is indicated by these lights at night?
bank.explanation: Green over white lights in a vertical line indicate a vessel engaged in trawling. Red over white would indicate fishing other than trawling
options: Vessel engaged in pilotage duty
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Vessel fishing (other than trawling)
Vessel engaged in trawling

bank.question: You are entering a UK harbour from the sea. Which description matches a Port Hand Lateral Mark in IALA Region A?
bank.explanation: When entering a harbour in the UK (IALA Region A), the Port Hand mark is red and has a cylindrical (can) topmark.
options: It is red and has a cylindrical (can) topmark.
It is green and has a conical topmark.
It is red and has a conical topmark.
It is green and has a cylindrical (can) topmark.

bank.question: A medium-sized motor cruiser at sea displaying two black spheres in a vertical line on its signal mast. What does this day shape configuration indicate about the vessel?
bank.explanation: Two black balls in a vertical line indicate a vessel 'Not Under Command' (NUC), meaning through exceptional circumstances she cannot manoeuvre as required
options: Vessel Not Under Command
Vessel Restricted in her Ability to Manoeuvre
Vessel Aground
Vessel engaged in underwater operations

bank.question: What is the correct VHF prefix for an 'Urgency' message, such as a broken-down vessel in a busy channel?
bank.explanation: Mayday is for 'grave and imminent danger' (life at risk). Pan-Pan is for urgent situations not involving immediate danger to life or the vessel
options: Securite
Mayday Relay
Pan-Pan
Mayday

bank.question: A close-up of an Admiralty chart showing a depth sounding of 12 meters with a small lowercase 'm' or uppercase 'M' nearby indicating seabed composition. What does the abbreviation 'M' indicate on a nautical chart regarding the seabed?
bank.explanation: The abbreviation 'M' on a chart stands for Mud. It is important to know this for choosing a suitable anchorage
options: Mixed bottom
Mud
Magnetism area
Marina ahead

bank.question: You need to put a fixed, non-slipping loop in a line to secure it over a harbour bollard. Which knot is most suitable?
bank.explanation: The Bowline is the standard knot used to form a secure, non-slipping loop at the end of a rope, ideal for securing to a bollard or ring.
options: Bowline knot
Figure-of-eight knot
Clove hitch
Sheet bend

bank.question: A pillar-shaped buoy with horizontal black and red bands, topped with two black spheres at the topmark. Identify this buoy?
bank.explanation: An isolated danger mark has two black spheres as a topmark. It is placed directly over a hazard that has navigable water all around it
options: Safe Water Mark
East Cardinal Mark
Isolated Danger Mark
Special Mark

bank.question: When sailing upwind, what is the 'Lee-bowing' technique used to achieve?
bank.explanation: Lee-bowing involves steering into the tide so the stream pushes the vessel toward the intended track, rather than away from it
options: Tacking as soon as the wind shifts against you
Positioning the vessel so the tidal stream hits the side of the bow to push you to windward
Sailing with the wind on the leeward side of the bow to increase speed
Dropping anchor to wait for the tide to turn before tacking

bank.question: A tall pillar buoy with red and white vertical stripes, featuring a single red sphere (ball) as the topmark. What is this buoy and what does it indicate?
bank.explanation: A safe water mark (red and white vertical stripes) has a single red ball as a topmark. Its light phase is often Isophase, Occulting, or a single Long Flash every 10s
options: Safe Water Mark
Port Hand Lateral Mark
Starboard Hand Lateral Mark
Emergency Wreck Buoy

bank.question: You are at sea at night and see the lights of another vessel. Which configuration indicates a power-driven vessel engaged in towing (length of tow under 200m) when seen from the side?
bank.explanation: Rule 24 states that a power-driven vessel towing (with a tow length under 200m) must show two masthead lights in a vertical line.
options: Two masthead lights in a vertical line.
Three masthead lights in a vertical line.
One masthead light and one towing light.
Only side lights and a stern light.

bank.question: A vessel at night displaying three all-round red lights in a vertical line. Sidelights and a masthead light are also visible. What is the status of a vessel displaying these three vertical red lights at night?
bank.explanation: Three vertical red lights indicate a vessel constrained by her draught. Memory aid: 'Three Reds, Not much water under my beds'
options: Vessel aground
Vessel not under command
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Vessel constrained by her draught

bank.question: On which point of sail is a sailing vessel most at risk of an 'accidental gybe'?
bank.explanation: A dead run is the most dangerous point of sail for an accidental gybe, which can cause injury or damage to the rig
options: Close hauled
Dead run
Beam reach
Broad reach

bank.question: A red, flat-topped (can) buoy floating in a channel. There are no topmarks. Identify this buoy and which side you should leave it on when heading into port?
bank.explanation: In IALA Region A (UK/Europe), a Port Hand mark is red and may be a can, pillar, or spar shape. When entering a harbour with the flood tide, you leave it to your port (left) side
options: Starboard Hand Mark - Leave to starboard when entering harbour
Port Hand Mark - Leave to port when entering harbour
Special Mark - Area of interest
Isolated Danger - Pass either side

bank.question: You are navigating near a dangerous wreck and need to pass to the North of it. Which cardinal mark indicates the North?
bank.explanation: A North Cardinal mark is identified by its topmark of two cones both pointing upwards (North).
options: A North Cardinal mark identified by its topmark of two cones both pointing upwards (North).
An East Cardinal mark with two cones pointing away from each other.
A South Cardinal mark with two cones pointing downwards.
A West Cardinal mark with two cones pointing towards each other.

bank.question: A bright yellow buoy (it can be any shape but usually spar or pillar) with a single yellow 'X' (cross) as the topmark. Identify this buoy based on its colour and topmark?
bank.explanation: A yellow cross indicates a Special Mark. These are used to mark features like racing buoys, outfalls, or cable areas, rather than navigation hazards
options: West Cardinal Mark
New Danger Mark
Special Mark
Safe Water Mark

bank.question: Using the 'Rule of Twelfths', what fraction of the tidal range is expected to rise during the third hour after Low Water?
bank.explanation: The Rule of Twelfths assumes a six-hour tidal cycle where the depth increases by 1/12, 2/12, 3/12, 3/12, 2/12, and 1/12 of the range per hour

bank.question: A dark night scene showing a vessel with a red light over a white light in a vertical line. A white sidelight is visible further back. Identify the activity of this vessel based on the vertical red and white lights?
bank.explanation: According to ColRegs Rule 26, a vessel fishing other than trawling (e.g., with nets/lines) displays Red over White lights. Red over White, Frying tonight!
options: Vessel fishing (other than trawling)
Vessel engaged in pilotage duty
Vessel at anchor
Sailing vessel under way

bank.question: Which day shape indicates a vessel 'Restricted in her Ability to Manoeuvre', such as one engaged in underwater operations?
bank.explanation: The V-shaped day shape (two cones, apexes pointing together) indicates a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre. Men at work or diving operations often use this signal.
options: A cylinder
Two cones, apexes pointing together (V-shaped)
A ball, a diamond, and a ball in a vertical line
Three balls in a vertical line

bank.question: A North Cardinal mark buoy with black over yellow horizontal bands and a topmark of two black cones both pointing upwards. On which side of this buoy is the safest water?
bank.explanation: A North Cardinal mark indicates that the safest water lies to the North of the buoy. Its topmark consists of two cones pointing upwards
options: To the South
To the East
To the North
To the West

bank.question: What is the primary difference between IALA Region A (UK) and IALA Region B lateral marks?
bank.explanation: The IALA A system (used in the UK/Europe) uses Red for Port and Green for Starboard; the reverse applies in IALA B (Americas/parts of Asia)
options: The colours are the same in both systems
Red marks the Port side in both systems
The colours of Port and Starboard marks are reversed between the two systems
The shapes are different, but the colours are the same

bank.question: A nautical chart extract showing a depth sounding of 4.5 metres with a thin horizontal line printed directly underneath the digits. What does the line under the depth sounding 4.5 indicate on an Admiralty chart?
bank.explanation: A depth with a line under it, or bracketed, indicates that the position of the sounding has shifted or is not in its surveyed position
options: Position of depth is doubtful
The area is drying at low water
Depth is in fathoms, not metres
The seabed is rocky at this point

bank.question: When plotting a course and accounting for both leeway and the set of the tide, what symbol represents an 'Estimated Position' (EP)?
bank.explanation: The Estimated Position (EP) is represented by a triangle around the fix, with the track line showing the water track plus the tide (indicated by 3 arrows).
options: A circle around the fix with a single arrow on the track line
A square around the fix with two arrows on the track line
A triangle around the fix with three arrows on the track line
A cross around the fix with no arrows on the track line

bank.question: A black cylinder day shape displayed prominently from the mast of a large vessel. What is the status of a vessel displaying this day shape?
bank.explanation: A vessel constrained by her draught must show three vertical red lights at night and a cylinder day shape
options: Vessel at anchor
Vessel constrained by her draught
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Vessel aground

bank.question: A vessel displays two black balls in a vertical line as a day shape. What does this indicate?
bank.explanation: Two black balls indicate a vessel 'Not Under Command' (NUC), meaning it cannot keep out of the way due to an exceptional circumstance
options: A vessel Not Under Command
A vessel Restricted in her Ability to Manoeuvre
A vessel aground
A vessel engaged in fishing

bank.question: A nautical chart symbol showing a magenta-coloured diamond shape containing the capital letter 'B'. What does this chart symbol indicate to a navigator?
bank.explanation: The symbol of a magenta diamond with a letter inside refers to a 'Tidal Diamond', with data found in the tidal marks table on the chart
options: A pilot boarding station
A dangerous wreck
A marine nature reserve
Tidal stream information is available for this position

bank.question: Which day shape must be displayed by a motor-sailing vessel (using both sails and engine) during the day?
bank.explanation: When a yacht is under sail but also using its engine, it is considered a power-driven vessel and must display a conical shape, apex downwards.
options: A ball
A cylinder
A diamond
A conical shape, apex downwards

bank.question: A nautical chart extract showing the abbreviation 'Co' on the seabed area. What does the seabed abbreviation 'Co' stand for?
bank.explanation: The symbol 'Co' on an Admiralty chart stands for Coral, which is a significant seabed feature
options: Coral
Cobbles
Coarse sand
Concrete blocks

bank.question: In a tidal stream atlas, what does the term 'Drift' refer to?
bank.explanation: The Drift is the speed of the tidal stream, while the Set is the direction in which it flows
options: The distance the vessel has travelled on its course
The direction in which the tide is flowing
The speed of the tidal stream in knots
The error caused by magnetic deviation

bank.question: A West Cardinal mark buoy, yellow with a single broad horizontal black band. The topmark is two black cones with their points together (pointing at each other). In which direction should you pass this buoy to remain in safe water?
bank.explanation: A West Cardinal mark has a black band in the middle and its cones point towards each other. To pass safely, you must stay to the West
options: To the North
To the East
To the West
To the South

bank.question: Which line on a boat, moored alongside in a marina, would be the 'Bow Spring' to prevent the boat from moving forward, especially with wind from astern?
bank.explanation: The bow spring runs from the bow of the vessel to a point further aft on the pontoon, preventing the boat from moving forward.
options: A line running from the bow to a point forward on the pontoon
A line running from the stern to a point forward on the pontoon
A line running from the bow to a point further aft on the pontoon
A line running from the stern to a point further aft on the pontoon

bank.question: The night-time lights of a vessel showing three vertical lights: Red at the top, White in the middle, and Red at the bottom. What is the status of a vessel displaying these vertical lights at night?
bank.explanation: A vessel 'Restricted in her Ability to Manoeuvre' (RAM) shows a red-white-red light configuration or a ball-diamond-ball day shape
options: Vessel aground
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Vessel constrained by her draught
Vessel engaged in fishing

bank.question: In which of the following scenarios is it appropriate to issue a 'Mayday' distress call?
bank.explanation: A Mayday call is reserved for situations where there is 'grave and imminent danger' to a vessel or persons
options: A vessel has run out of fuel in calm weather
A vessel is taking on water and is in danger of sinking
A crew member has a minor cut and needs medical advice
A vessel has a fouled propeller but is at safe anchor

bank.question: A yellow buoy, pillar-shaped, with a yellow 'X' shaped topmark. Identify this buoy and its general purpose?
bank.explanation: A flashing yellow light (usually 2 seconds on, 2 seconds off) on a Special Mark identifies a specific area such as a race course or outfall
options: Special Mark indicating a specific feature (e.g. outfall or spoil ground)
Isolated Danger mark
Preferred Channel mark to Starboard
Emergency Wreck Buoy

bank.question: When identifying a light on a chart labelled 'Iso W 4s', which timing characteristic represents an Isophase light?
bank.explanation: An Isophase light has equal periods of light and darkness, as shown by the perfectly balanced 2s on/2s off pattern.
options: A light with a single, long flash followed by a period of darkness
A light with equal periods of light and darkness
A light with several short flashes in quick succession
A light that rapidly alternates between red and white

bank.question: A pillar-shaped buoy with vertical red and white stripes and a single red spherical topmark. What type of buoy is this, often used to indicate the start of a channel?
bank.explanation: A Safe Water Mark, with vertical red/white stripes, can be used as a 'Landfall' mark to indicate the start of a buoyed channel
options: Port Hand Mark
Starboard Hand Mark
Isolated Danger Mark
Safe Water Mark

bank.question: In a shipping forecast, what does the term 'Backing' mean regarding wind direction?
bank.explanation: A 'Backing' wind changes direction in an anti-clockwise direction (e.g., from West to South-West)
options: Anti-clockwise
Clockwise
Increasing in speed
Decreasing in speed

bank.question: A buoy with horizontal black and red bands and a topmark consisting of two black spheres/balls. What is the name of this buoy?
bank.explanation: An isolated danger mark is placed over a hazard that has navigable water all around it. It is black with one or more red horizontal bands
options: Fairway Mark
North Cardinal Mark
Isolated Danger Mark
New Danger Mark

bank.question: Which buoy, characterised by vertical red and white stripes and a single red sphere topmark, indicates a 'Fairway' or 'Landfall' where there is safe water all around?
bank.explanation: A Safe Water Mark, characterised by vertical red and white stripes and a single red sphere topmark, indicates there is navigable water all around the buoy.
options: A lateral mark
A special mark
A cardinal mark
A safe water mark

bank.question: A green conical-shaped buoy, used as an IALA Region A Starboard hand mark. Heading into a UK harbour (with the flood), on which side of the boat should you leave this mark?
bank.explanation: A green buoy with a conical shape is a Starboard Hand mark. When entering a harbour (direction of buoyage), it should be left to starboard (the right side)
options: Port side (Left)
Starboard side (Right)
Either side
Do not pass

bank.question: What is the correct topmark for a South Cardinal buoy?
bank.explanation: South Cardinal marks are yellow on top, black on the bottom, with two downward-pointing cones. They must be passed to the South
options: Two cones, points together (diamond shape)
Two cones, points facing upwards
Two cones, points facing outwards (hourglass shape)
Two cones, points facing downwards

bank.question: A black conical day shape, pointing downwards, displayed on the forestay of a sailing vessel. What does this day shape indicate when displayed on a sailing vessel?
bank.explanation: A yacht under power with sails up is considered a power-driven vessel and must display a conical shape, point down, in the forward part where it can best be seen
options: Vessel is at anchor
Vessel is fishing
Vessel is motorsailing (under power and sail)
Vessel is a pilot boat

bank.question: According to IRPCS Rule 12, if two sailing vessels on the same tack (Starboard Tack) are on a collision course, which vessel is the 'Stand-on vessel'?
bank.explanation: According to IRPCS Rule 12, when two sailing vessels have the wind on the same side, the vessel to windward must keep out of the way of the vessel to leeward.
options: The vessel to windward
The vessel to leeward
The vessel with the most experienced crew
The vessel with the smaller sails

bank.question: A diagram of a vessel's mast displaying three black day shapes in a vertical line: a ball at the top, a diamond in the middle, and a ball at the bottom. What is the status of a vessel displaying these three day shapes in a vertical line?
bank.explanation: A black ball over a black diamond over a black ball indicates a vessel restricted in her ability to manuvre
options: Vessel at anchor
Vessel constrained by draught
Vessel restricted in her ability to manuvre
Vessel aground

bank.question: In navigation, what does the term 'Variation' define?
bank.explanation: Variation is the angle between True North and Magnetic North, which changes depending on location and year
options: The difference between Magnetic North and Compass North
The effect of iron or electronics near the compass
The difference between True North and Magnetic North
The difference between High Water and Low Water heights

bank.question: A North Cardinal pillar buoy with a topmark of two black cones pointing upwards. The top half of the buoy is black and the bottom half is yellow. To remain in safe water, on which side (Compass direction) should you pass this buoy?
bank.explanation: A yellow and black buoy with two cones pointing upwards is a North Cardinal mark; you must pass to the North
options: North
South
East
West

bank.question: Which visual navigation aid is formed when two fixed objects on the chart are observed to be perfectly in line, providing a very accurate position line?
bank.explanation: A transit (or range) is formed when two fixed objects on the chart are observed to be perfectly in line, providing a very accurate position line.
options: An estimated position
A transfer bearing
A transit or leading line
A running fix

bank.question: A snippet of a nautical chart showing a depth sounding with the capital letter 'W' printed underneath it. What does the abbreviation 'W' indicate on a nautical chart regarding the seabed?
bank.explanation: An uppercase 'W' on an Admiralty chart indicates a seabed composed of Seaweed
options: White sand
Seaweed
Wreck nearby
West cardinal mark

bank.question: What type of weather is most commonly associated with a High Pressure 'Anticyclone'?
bank.explanation: High pressure systems (Anticyclones) generally bring settled weather with light winds and clear skies
options: Strong winds and heavy rain
Settled weather with light winds and clear skies
Rapidly falling barometric pressure
Fast-moving cold fronts and squalls

bank.question: A red port hand lateral buoy with a cylindrical (can) topmark. When entering a harbour in the UK, what does this buoy indicate?
bank.explanation: A cylinder topmark on a red port lateral mark indicates the port side of the channel when returning to harbour (IALA A)
options: Starboard side of the channel
Mid-channel mark
Isolated danger mark
Port side of the channel

bank.question: When approaching a rocky outcrop and needing to pass to the West of the danger, which cardinal mark would you look for?
bank.explanation: A West Cardinal mark indicates safe water to the West of the hazard and is identified by two cones point-to-point.
options: An East Cardinal Mark
A South Cardinal Mark
A West Cardinal Mark
A North Cardinal Mark

bank.question: A black cone day shape displayed on the forestay of a yacht, with the apex (point) pointing downwards. What does this day shape indicate when displayed on a yacht?
bank.explanation: A sailing vessel under engine power is treated as a power-driven vessel and must display a cone, apex down
options: A sailing vessel also propelled by machinery
A vessel fishing with gear extended
A vessel under sail only
A pilot vessel on duty

bank.question: If a chart shows a depth of 5m and the height of tide is 3m, what is the actual depth of water?
bank.explanation: Depth = (Charted Depth) + (Tide Height). So, 5m + 3m = 8m
options: 8 Metres
2 Metres
5 Metres
3 Metres

bank.question: A pillar buoy with equal vertical stripes of blue and yellow, topped with a yellow upright cross. What is the purpose of this specifically coloured blue and yellow buoy?
bank.explanation: A blue and yellow buoy usually indicates an emergency wreck mark, used for newly discovered dangers
options: Special Mark
Emergency Wreck Mark
Fairway Mark
Safe Water Mark

bank.question: In RYA navigation, which line symbol specifically represents the Course to Steer (CTS) after correcting for tidal stream and leeway?
bank.explanation: In RYA navigation, a line with two arrows indicates the Course to Steer (CTS) after correcting for tide and leeway.
options: A single arrowed line
A line with two arrows
A dashed line
A dotted line

bank.question: A night-time view showing two red all-round lights in a vertical line on a vessel's mast. No other lights are visible. What does this light configuration indicate at night?
bank.explanation: Two red lights in a vertical line indicate a vessel 'Not Under Command' (NUC), unable to manuvre
options: Vessel at anchor
Vessel engaged in pilotage
Vessel not under command
Vessel constrained by her draught

bank.question: Under COLREGs, what does a single short blast on the whistle mean?
bank.explanation: One short blast (one second) indicates 'I am altering my course to starboard'
options: I am altering my course to port
I am operating astern propulsion
I am altering my course to starboard
I am stationary and making no way through the water

bank.question: A compass rose from a nautical chart showing a variation of 2 degrees 15' W in 2015, with an annual change of 8' E. What does this information found in the centre of a chart's compass rose represent?
bank.explanation: Mag Var (Magnetic Variation) is the difference between calculations based on True North and Magnetic North
options: Magnetic Variation
Magnetic Deviation_now
Grid North offset
Tidal stream direction

bank.question: According to COLREGs, when two power-driven vessels are meeting on reciprocal or nearly reciprocal courses, how should they avoid a collision?
bank.explanation: According to COLREGs Rule 14, when two power-driven vessels are meeting on reciprocal courses so as to involve risk of collision, each shall alter course to starboard so each shall pass on the port side of the other
options: Alter course to port to pass starboard-to-starboard
Alter course to starboard to pass port-to-port
The larger vessel stands on while the smaller vessel gives way
The vessel with the wind on its port side gives way

bank.question: A yellow pillar-shaped buoy with a yellow 'X' (St Andrew's Cross) topmark. Identify this buoy?
bank.explanation: A yellow buoy with an 'X' topmark is a Special Mark, used to indicate areas like racing marks or outfalls
options: Safe Water Mark
Lateral Mark
Isolated Danger Mark
Special Mark

bank.question: What are 'Spring Tides'?
bank.explanation: Spring tides occur when the gravitational pull of the Sun and Moon are in alignment (New or Full Moon), resulting in the highest high waters and lowest low waters
options: Tides with the smallest range in the lunar cycle
Tides that occur only in the spring season
Tides with the greatest range between high and low water
Tides that occur when the Moon is at a right angle to the Sun

bank.question: A chart symbol for a lighthouse with the text 'Int.Q.R.10s' printed beside it. In the light description 'Int.Q.R.10s', what does 'Int' stand for?
bank.explanation: The 'Int' prefix on a lighthouse description stands for 'Interrupted Quick' flashing
options: International Quality light
Interrupted Quick flashing light
Intense Quartz light
Internal Quiet period

bank.question: What is the topmark for an Isolated Danger Mark?
bank.explanation: An Isolated Danger mark is placed over a specific hazard with navigable water all around it. Its topmark consists of two black spheres
options: Two black spheres
Two black cones pointing upwards
A single red sphere
A black 'X' shape

bank.question: An Isolated Danger buoy with black and red horizontal bands and two black spheres (balls) as a topmark. Identify this buoy and its topmark configuration?
bank.explanation: Two black balls in a vertical line represent an isolated danger mark, indicating navigable water all around but a hazard at the spot
options: Safe Water Mark
South Cardinal Mark house
Isolated Danger Mark house
Port Hand Mark house

bank.question: What is the primary purpose of a 'Clearing Bearing' in pilotage?
bank.explanation: A clearing bearing is a safety limit plotted on a chart to ensure a vessel stays in safe water and avoids a specific hazard like a rock or shallow patch
options: A bearing taken to confirm the vessel's speed over ground
A line used to identify when a vessel is exactly halfway to its destination
A bearing used to calculate the exact distance to a lighthouse
A bearing used to define the boundary between safe water and a hazard

bank.question: A black diamond day shape displayed on a vessel. What does this black diamond day shape indicate when seen on a tug or its tow?
bank.explanation: A diamond shape indicates a vessel being towed if the length of the tow exceeds 200 metres
options: A tow exceeding 200m in length
A vessel engaged in diving operations
A vessel at anchor
A vessel restricted in its ability to manuvre

bank.question: In navigation, what is 'Deviation'?
bank.explanation: Magnetic Deviation is the error introduced by local magnetic fields on the boat itself, such as the engine, wiring, or metal equipment, affecting the compass needle
options: The difference between True North and Magnetic North based on geography
The error caused by magnetic influences on the vessel itself
The sideways movement of a vessel caused by the wind
The difference between the vessel's heading and its track over ground

bank.question: A single black cylinder day shape displayed vertically on a vessel. What is the status of a vessel displaying this black cylinder day shape?
bank.explanation: A vessel displaying a cylinder day shape is constrained by its draught, meaning it is severely restricted in its ability to deviate from its course due to the depth of water
options: Vessel at anchor
Vessel constrained by draught
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Vessel engaged in fishing

bank.question: What is the generally accepted value for average atmospheric pressure at sea level?
bank.explanation: The standard pressure at sea level is approximately 1013 hPa. Readings significantly higher indicate high pressure, and lower indicate low pressure
options: 990 HPa
1000 HPa
1013 HPa
1025 HPa

bank.question: An East Cardinal buoy with black bands at the top and bottom and a yellow band in the middle. The topmark consists of two black cones pointing away from each other (base to base). Identify this cardinal mark?
bank.explanation: The topmarks (two cones pointing away from each other) and the black-yellow-black horizontal bands identify this as an East Cardinal mark
options: North Cardinal
South Cardinal
East Cardinal
West Cardinal

bank.question: What are the characteristics of a Port Hand lateral mark in IALA Region A?
bank.explanation: A Port Hand lateral mark in IALA Region A is red in colour, has a 'can' shape, and if it carries a light, it must be red
options: Red colour, can-shaped, red light
Green colour, conical-shaped, green light
Red and white stripes, spherical-shaped, white light
Yellow and black, pillar-shaped, white light

bank.question: A pillar buoy with vertical red and white stripes and a single red sphere as a topmark. What type of buoy is this, indicating that there is navigable water all around it?
bank.explanation: Red and white vertical stripes with a single red ball topmark identify a Safe Water Mark, which indicates navigable water all around
options: Safe Water Mark
Isolated Danger Mark
Emergency Wreck Buoy
Special Mark

bank.question: What is the light sequence for a North Cardinal mark?
bank.explanation: A North Cardinal mark has two cones pointing upwards. The light sequence is a continuous quick or very quick white flash to distinguish it from the timed groups of other cardinals
options: 3 Flashes every 10 seconds
6 Flashes + 1 long flash every 15 seconds
9 Flashes every 15 seconds
Continuous quick or very quick white flashes

bank.question: A night-time view showing two red lights arranged in a vertical line on a vessel's mast. At night, what does a vessel displaying these two vertical red lights indicate?
bank.explanation: Two vertical red lights signify a vessel 'Not Under Command,' meaning it cannot manoeuvre as required by the rules due to some exceptional circumstance
options: Vessel at anchor
Vessel aground
Vessel not under command
Pilot vessel on duty

bank.question: What is the function of the 'Distress' button on a DSC-enabled VHF radio?
bank.explanation: The DSC 'Distress' button sends an automated digital alert to the Coastguard and all nearby vessels, including your MMSI and coordinates if linked to a GPS
options: It sends a text message to the ship's owner
It sends an automated digital distress alert to all stations including GPS position
It activates the vessel's EPIRB via satellite
It automatically steers the boat toward the nearest harbour

bank.question: A snippet of a nautical chart showing a depth sounding with the lowercase letter 'm' underneath it. What does the seabed abbreviation 'm' indicate on a nautical chart?
bank.explanation: The abbreviation 'm' stands for mud, which is a soft type of seabed material often found in estuaries
options: Mixed ground
Mud
Mussels
Medium sand
